title: SEEK: Skill Extraction with Evolving Knowledge against Frontier Science Agents
abstract: arXiv:2610.34365v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Science agents increasingly package domain expertise as reusable skills that plan analyses, select tools, and execute workflows. This modularity creates a confidentiality risk: the interactions that deliver a skill's capability can also reveal the skill itself. We build an extensible benchmark of 40 protected skills across eight open- and closed-source science-agent platforms, comparing direct, fixed-strategy, and bandit-guided iterative probing under reference-based and reference-free evaluation. Leakage is pervasive: all eight platforms (100%) leak at least one protected skill, and four reach 100% attack success under a single direct request. To stress-test platforms that resist simple probing, we propose SEEK (Skill Extraction with Evolving Knowledge), a black-box, self-evolving red-teaming agent that consolidates response-derived evidence in persistent memory and evolves reusable attack skills, using only user-visible responses. translated_title: SEEK：面向前沿科学智能体的基于演化知识的技能提取方法
translated_abstract: arXiv:2610.34365v1 公告类型：交叉  摘要：科学智能体日益将其领域专业知识封装为可复用的技能，用于规划分析、选择工具和执行工作流程。这种模块化设计带来了保密性风险：传递技能能力的交互过程也可能暴露技能本身。我们构建了一个可扩展的基准测试，涵盖八个开源与闭源科学智能体平台上的40个受保护技能，并在基于参考和无参考的评估下比较了直接探测、固定策略和老虎机引导的迭代探测方法。技能泄露现象普遍存在：全部八个平台（100%）至少泄露一个受保护技能，其中四个平台在单次直接请求下即达到100%的攻击成功率。为了对能够抵御简单探测的平台进行压力测试，我们提出了SEEK（基于演化知识的技能提取），这是一个黑盒、自演化的红队攻击智能体，它仅利用用户可见的响应，在持久记忆中整合从响应中获取的证据，并演化出可复用的攻击技能。在
tldr: 本文提出了SEEK，一个黑盒自演化红队攻击智能体，通过在持久记忆中整合响应证据并演化可复用攻击技能，成功提取了科学智能体平台中受保护的技能，揭示了100%测试平台均存在技能泄露的严重安全风险。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes SEEK, a black-box self-evolving red-teaming agent that consolidates response-derived evidence in persistent memory and evolves reusable attack skills, successfully extracting protected skills from science-agent platforms and revealing severe security risks with 100% of tested platforms leaking at least one skill.
